Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump attend a trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Leaders’ Summit in Shenzhen, China, November 19, 2026. | Photo Credit: Sputnik via Reuters
India said it had “taken note” of the trilateral summit of the leaders of the U.S., Russia and China in Shenzhen , held on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Conference (APEC). In its first comments on the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping that has been dubbed a “G-3”, the Ministry of External Affairs was non-committal.
“We have taken note of this meeting between three APEC member countries,” said the Ministry’s spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, responding to a question at a briefing on Friday (November 20, 2026). “We await a fuller account of the concrete outcomes of this meeting before offering our assessment,” he added.
The trilateral summit ended with a joint statement that described the meeting as “historic”.
“We will be having discussions on the theme of upholding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major country relations. Peace has been an enduring pursuit of humanity. Our planet has been put through more than 10,000 wars,” the host, Mr. Xi said, calling the trilateral summit a “groundbreaking move”.
The joint statement issued in Washington, Moscow, and Beijing highlighted four areas of cooperation for the three countries, including reform of the United Nations, increasing the production and supply of petroleum products, curtailing the actions of the International Criminal Court and other international agencies that violated the immunity of State officials, and nuclear arms control and preventing proliferation.
The Opposition had criticised the government, suggesting that India should have been included in the summit where global issues were being discussed. “If the Congress were in power, India’s Prime Minister would be sitting at this table ,” Congress leader Rahul Gandhi posted on social media, with a photograph of Mr. Trump, Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin around a table in Shenzhen. India is not a member of the 21-nation APEC grouping, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi had met Mr. Trump on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) at the Quad summit in Manila.
“There were some concrete outcomes which came out of [the Quad Summit] including the Quad Business Leaders Forum which is to be held next year,” Mr. Jaiswal said, listing initiatives announced after the Quad meeting, including on emerging technologies, maritime surveillance, cybersecurity cooperation and security issues.
“These decisions are [examples of] practical cooperation that is delivering for the people and countries in the Indo-Pacific region,” Mr. Jaiswal added.
